easy.def: To have a certain look, place, or feeling.
examples: I am happy today.
The cat is on the bed.
We were at the park.

more.def: To exist, to stay in a place, or to have a certain quality.
examples: The library is next to the school.
Our teacher was late this morning because of the snow.
Whales are the largest animals on Earth.

easy.def: Sandy land next to the sea.
examples: We play on the beach.
The beach is sandy.
We built a castle on the beach.

more.def: A sandy or pebbly area beside the sea or a lake.
examples: We collected shells on the beach.
Waves washed over the sandy beach.
A lifeguard watched the beach.

easy.def: A big strong animal with thick fur.
examples: The bear sleeps all winter.
Bears like honey.
A brown bear walked by the stream.

more.def: A large, heavy animal with thick fur and sharp claws.
examples: The bear caught a fish in the stream.
A polar bear lives in the cold north.
Black bears climb trees.

easy.def: To put up with something.
examples: I cannot bear the noise.
She bears the cold well.
He could not bear to wait.

more.def: To put up with something unpleasant.
examples: I cannot bear the loud noise.
She bore the cold without complaining.
He could not bear to see the puppy sad.

easy.def: To win against someone.
examples: Our team beat the red team.
I beat my dad at checkers.
She beat me in a race.

more.def: To win against someone in a game or contest.
examples: Our team beat the other school by two points.
He beat his sister at chess for the first time.
The turtle beat the hare in the old story.

easy.def: To hit again and again.
examples: Rain beat on the roof.
Beat the drum.
The waves beat on the rocks.

more.def: To hit something over and over.
examples: The drummer beat the drum in a steady rhythm.
Rain beat against the tent all night.
Beat the eggs with a whisk until they are fluffy.

easy.def: The steady pulse of music.
examples: Clap to the beat.
The song has a fast beat.
I can feel the beat of my heart.

more.def: The regular, steady pattern of sound in music, or in your heart.
examples: The dancers moved in time with the beat of the drum.
Clap along to the beat of the song.
You can feel the beat of your heart when you run.

easy.def: Very nice to look at or hear.
examples: What a beautiful flower!
The sunset is beautiful.
You made a beautiful card.

more.def: Very pleasing to see, hear, or think about.
examples: The beautiful music made everyone stop and listen.
The garden looked beautiful after the roses bloomed.
She has a beautiful singing voice.

easy.def: Being very nice to look at.
examples: I love the beauty of the sunset.
The beauty of the garden.
She admired the beauty of the lake.

more.def: The quality of being very pleasing to look at or hear.
examples: We admired the beauty of the mountains.
The beauty of the song made her smile.
The garden was full of beauty in spring.

easy.def: A word used to give a reason.
examples: I am happy because it is my birthday.
We stayed in because it rained.
She cried because she fell.

more.def: A word used to tell the reason for something.
examples: The ice melted because the sun was so hot.
I wore a sweater because the room was cold.
He could not play because his leg hurt.

easy.def: To grow or change into something.
examples: A tadpole becomes a frog.
The sky became dark.
She became a nurse.

more.def: To start to be something, or to change into something different.
examples: A caterpillar will become a butterfly.
The sky became dark as the storm moved in.
He wants to become a pilot when he grows up.

easy.def: A soft place where you sleep.
examples: I go to bed at eight.
My cat sleeps on my bed.
Make your bed in the morning.

more.def: A piece of furniture with a mattress where people lie down to sleep or rest.
examples: The hotel room had two beds and a view of the sea.
I read a story every night before bed.
The nurse made the bed with clean sheets.

easy.def: A piece of ground where plants grow.
examples: We planted tulips in the flower bed.
The garden bed is full of carrots.
Weeds grew in the bed.

more.def: A small area of ground where flowers or vegetables are planted.
examples: Dad dug a new bed for the tomato plants.
Heavy rain washed the seeds out of the flower bed.
Weeds had grown in the vegetable bed all summer.

easy.def: A room where you sleep.
examples: My bedroom is upstairs.
I read in my bedroom.
The bedroom has a bed.

more.def: A room in a home where people sleep.
examples: My bedroom is at the top of the stairs.
She decorated her bedroom with posters.
The house has three bedrooms.

easy.def: A bubbly drink that only adults may have.
examples: Adults may drink beer.
Dad had a beer.
Beer is for grown-ups.

more.def: A bubbly drink made from grain that only adults may drink.
examples: He ordered a glass of beer with dinner.
Beer is sold only to adults.
Dad poured a beer at the barbecue.

easy.def: Earlier than something else.
examples: Wash up before dinner.
I woke before the sun.
Brush your teeth before bed.

more.def: At an earlier time than something else, or in front of something.
examples: Please finish your homework before you play outside.
The thunder came before the rain.
He arrived at the station before noon.

easy.def: At an earlier time.
examples: I have seen it before.
She came the day before.
Have you been here before?

more.def: At some time earlier than now.
examples: I have never ridden a horse before.
We met the new teacher the day before.
Have you tried this fruit before?

easy.def: To ask for something very much.
examples: The puppy begs for a treat.
I begged Mom for a pet.
He begged to stay.

more.def: To ask for something in a strong, pleading way.
examples: The puppy begged for a bite of my sandwich.
She begged her parents to let her stay up late.
The child begged to go on the ride again.

easy.def: To start.
examples: Class begins at nine.
We began to sing.
The show will begin soon.

more.def: To start doing something, or to happen for the first time.
examples: School begins at eight o'clock.
She began to paint when she was six.
The race begins when the whistle blows.

easy.def: The start of something.
examples: The beginning of the book is funny.
The beginning of the race.
At the beginning, it is easy.

more.def: The first part of something, or the time when it starts.
examples: The beginning of the movie was funny.
At the beginning of the year, we met our teacher.
Spring is the beginning of the growing season.

easy.def: At the back of something.
examples: The cat hid behind the couch.
Stand behind me in line.
The sun went behind a cloud.

more.def: At the back of something, or following after it.
examples: A rabbit hid behind the bushes in the garden.
The young ducks swam in a line behind their mother.
The sun slipped behind the mountains at the end of the day.

easy.def: Not as far along as others.
examples: The last runner fell behind.
I am behind in my reading.
Our team is behind now, but we can still win.

more.def: Farther back or less far along than others, or than planned.
examples: The hikers at the back of the group fell behind on the steep trail.
She was behind at halftime, but she scored three times and won.
I am a little behind in math because I was sick.

easy.def: To think that something is true.
examples: I believe you.
I believe it will snow soon.
Do you believe in fairies?

more.def: To feel sure that something is true or real.
examples: She believed her team could win if they worked together.
Nobody believed him when he said he saw a bear.
I believe that practice will make me a better swimmer.

easy.def: A metal cup that rings when it is hit.
examples: The bell rings.
Ring the bell.
The school bell is loud.

more.def: A hollow metal object that makes a ringing sound when it is struck.
examples: The school bell rings at the end of the day.
A bell hung from the church tower.
The cat wore a tiny bell on its collar.

easy.def: To be owned by someone.
examples: This book belongs to me.
The coat belongs to Sam.
Who does the toy belong to?

more.def: To be the property of a person or group, or to be owned by them.
examples: This pencil belongs to Mia.
The bike belongs to my sister.
Who does this coat belong to?

easy.def: To be in the right place.
examples: The shoes belong by the door.
Books belong on the shelf.
The spoon belongs in the drawer.

more.def: To be in the right place or group.
examples: Pencils belong in the desk, not on the floor.
A penguin belongs in cold places.
You belong on our team.

easy.def: A strip you wear around your waist.
examples: My belt holds up my pants.
He wears a belt.
The belt is brown.

more.def: A strip of leather or cloth worn around the waist.
examples: His belt had a shiny buckle.
He fastened his belt tight.
A brown leather belt held the tools.

easy.def: A loop that moves things.
examples: The belt carries bags.
The fan belt.
The belt moves boxes.

more.def: A loop of material that moves around wheels to carry or turn things.
examples: The belt carries bags at the airport.
A belt turns the wheels in the machine.
Boxes ride along the conveyor belt.

easy.def: Under.
examples: The cat is beneath the table.
The fish swim beneath the boat.
I hid beneath my blanket.

more.def: Under or below something.
examples: The treasure was buried beneath an old oak tree.
Worms tunnel beneath the surface of the soil.
We sat beneath a shady tree to eat our lunch.

easy.def: Better than all the others.
examples: She is my best friend.
This is the best cake.
He is the best runner.

more.def: Better than all the rest, or of the highest quality.
examples: The best part of the trip was seeing the dolphins.
She is the best swimmer on our team.
This is the best book I have read this year.

easy.def: In the most good way.
examples: I like this best.
She sings best.
He jumps the best.

more.def: In the most successful or pleasing way.
examples: Of all the paints, I like the blue one best.
The plants grow best in warm sunshine.
She did best on the spelling test.

easy.def: To say you feel sure.
examples: I bet it will rain today.
I bet you are hungry.
I bet she finds the lost key.

more.def: To say that you strongly believe something is true.
examples: I bet the bus is late because of the snow.
My brother bet that his team would win the game.
She bet that nobody could guess the answer to her riddle.

easy.def: A promise that the one who guesses wrong gives something.
examples: I made a bet with my brother.
Dad lost the bet.
Their bet was a cookie.

more.def: An agreement that the person who guesses wrong will give something to the other person.
examples: My sister won the bet, so I had to wash the dishes.
The two friends made a bet about which team would score first.
He lost the bet and had to carry his friend's backpack.

easy.def: More good than before or than another.
examples: This book is better.
I feel better now.
Her drawing is better than mine.

more.def: Of a higher quality than something else, or in improved health.
examples: Fresh bread is much better than stale bread.
I felt better after I rested for a day.
Practice will make your piano playing better.

easy.def: In a more good way.
examples: I sing better now.
She runs better than me.
Do it better next time.

more.def: In a more skillful or more pleasing way.
examples: My little sister reads better every week.
The plants grow better in the sun than in the shade.
You will do better on the test if you study.

easy.def: In the middle of two things.
examples: The cat sat between us.
The park is between two streets.
Put a pillow between the dolls.

more.def: In the space that separates two people, places or things.
examples: A small stream runs between the two hills.
My house is between the library and the bakery.
She stood between her two brothers in the photograph.

easy.def: Shared by two or more.
examples: Share the cookie between you two.
Divide the candy between the three of us.
The secret is between you and me.

more.def: Shared by, or connecting, two or more people or things.
examples: The twins split the pizza between them.
There is a strong friendship between the two dogs.
What is the difference between a frog and a toad?

easy.def: On the far side of something.
examples: The farm is beyond the hill.
Look beyond the trees.
The lake is beyond the woods.

more.def: On or to the far side of something.
examples: The farm is just beyond the hill.
A lake lies beyond the trees.
The path goes beyond the fence.
